findings.claim: ADR-0016's dynamic deny-reason text and the 'more:' follow-up line are shown to a model exactly like a tool description, but ADR-0005's lint rules (PR1 caps, PR2 doubt/default, PR5 pseudo-tags, PR7 length) never cover them, and lint.mjs has no code path that checks them.
findings.evidence: ADR-0005 scope line says 'Every prompt text (instructions and tool descriptions) follows these rules', but docs/v2/prompt/lint.mjs only has two modes: 'drafts' (parses docs/v2/prompt/drafts.md id blocks) and 'files' (counts caps/doubt/tags over given files). Neither mode takes ADR-0016's deny-reason template or the dynamic 'more: node <bundle>/search.mjs ...' line (docs/v2/adr/0016-subagent-context-protection.md case B, lines ~27, 50, 58) as input, and drafts.md has no id block for it.
findings.fix: Add the deny-reason template and the 'more:' line template as a drafts.md id block (or a second lint target) so lint.mjs checks them against PR1/PR2/PR5/PR7 like any other model-facing text.
findings.archaeology: n/a — this is a doc/process gap in v2 tooling, not a behavior inherited from v1 code, so git archaeology on v1 cm-main does not apply.

findings.claim: ctx_route is referenced only inside review workflow scripts (review-army.workflow.js, review-army-r4.workflow.js) as a reviewer-focus label; it has no definition anywhere in TECH-SPEC.md, ADR-0007, or ADR-0008, which confirms (does not overturn) r2/r4a finding #72/#36 that ctx_route's listed-vs-hidden status and its tools/list membership were never decided in any ADR.
findings.evidence: grep for ctx_route across docs/v2/TECH-SPEC.md and docs/v2/adr/0007-mcp-2026-07-28.md and docs/v2/adr/0008-enforcement-rewrite-and-cap.md returns zero hits; it appears only in docs/v2/review/review-army*.workflow.js and past review/out JSON files.
findings.fix: No new fix needed beyond r2/r4a's existing fix (decide listed vs hidden in ADR-0007/0008); recorded here only to confirm pass A's finding is correct, not to repeat it as new.
findings.archaeology: n/a — confirmation only, not a new claim about code behavior.
